correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the simple continuous null to iid uniforms, represents Cramér–von Mises and Watson as two quadratic forms of the same empirical-process sum, and applies an exact iid fourth-moment identity. Direct integration of the bridge kernel gives tr(Sigma^2)=1/90, tr(Sigma P Sigma)=1/360, and tr(Sigma P Sigma P)=1/720. For one uniform observation the projected quadratic form is identically 1/12, eliminating the non-Gaussian correction for Watson and the cross term. An independent exact-rational order-statistic integration verifies the resulting finite formulas through n=8.

originality.rationale: The closest full classical paper jointly devoted to the two statistics, Pearson--Stephens (1962), gives finite Cramér–von Mises moments, Monte Carlo Watson distributions, and marginal asymptotic cumulant relations but no finite joint covariance or correlation. A modern full treatment of both marginal limiting families likewise contains no correlation statement. Targeted semantic and web searches found no formula matching the finite-sample covariance or correlation.
residual_risks: Watson's 1961 article was not available in full during this run, so an explicit early joint moment there cannot be ruled out directly.
Older goodness-of-fit literature is extensive, and the same formula could have been recorded in a table or under alternate notation.
The result applies only to fully specified continuous nulls; fitted-parameter versions can have different covariance structure.

value.rationale: Cramér–von Mises and Watson are standard companion quadratic goodness-of-fit statistics. Exact finite-sample dependence is directly relevant to joint simulation, combined testing, benchmarking, and understanding redundancy. The closed correlation sqrt(2(n-1)/(4n-3)) and persistent 1/sqrt(2) limit are structurally informative and not recoverable from the well-known marginal distributions alone.
